setlist.title: It Must Have Been the Roses

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Crazy Fingers** (7 reviews): Runs about fifteen minutes; Brings out especially mournful vocals from Jerry [5][7][9][10][11][13][14]
- **Morning Dew** (2 reviews): Described as a very cozy closing number; Rare encore choice [7][11]
- **Peggy-O** (1 review): Singled out as a beautiful version, the reviewer's favorite [13]
- **Scarlet Begonias *(SBD only)** (1 review): Reviewer praises nice jamming [12]

## The recordings

- **gd1976-09-30.137537.mtx.dusborne.flac16** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 23 songs; 173 min; rated 3.2/5 by 5 [1]
- **gd76-09-30.fob-patched.unknown.11939.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 22 songs; 171 min; rated 3.5/5 by 8 [2]. Said about its sound: Reviewer finds the audience recording's sound good, surprisingly so [5]
- **gd1976-09-30.sbd.gans-cribbs.30225.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 16 songs; 113 min; rated 3/5 by 10 [3]
- **gd1976-09-30.sbd.18107.shnf**: soundboard; 7 songs; 56 min; rated 3.73/5 by 15 [4]. Said about its sound: Soundboard sounds cozy, though cleaner boards exist; small venues likely helped; Soundboard sound seems a little iffy in places; A few sound glitches [7][9][14]

## Around the show

- Show was originally scheduled for Mershon Auditorium but moved to St. John Arena, a roughly 12,000-seat basketball venue [8]
- Band was booked for a larger hall, but weak ticket sales moved it to Mershon, with general admission seating [15]
- Reviewer attended; early Deadbase had only a partial setlist and the tape was long elusive [15]
- Contains only first-disc and third-disc material; Disc 2 tracks are absent and found in Charlie Miller's seed [3]
- Reviewer calls it one of several outstanding Columbus, Ohio shows [8]
- Not the year's best show, but holds up well among thirty years of shows [14]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1976-09-30.137537.mtx.dusborne.flac16**: transferred by Matrix by Dave Usborne; source: 3 Source Matrix by Dusborne; Soundboard (shnid:030225+018107), Disc 1 & 3 [1]. Also: Matrix recording, credited to Dusborne, in 16-bit FLAC [1]
- **gd76-09-30.fob-patched.unknown.11939.sbeok.shnf**: source: Audience Recording [2]. Also: Audience master cassette to cassette to DAT to CD; Scarlet comes from a soundboard reel; via Jonathan Miller, seeded by Dave Backus [2]
- **gd1976-09-30.sbd.gans-cribbs.30225.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Andy Lemieux and Sean Cribbs; source: SBD>MR>DAT>CD [3]. Also: Soundboard from Gans with same lineage as other seed, without Sonic Solutions editing; master reel to DAT to CD to SHN [3]
- **gd1976-09-30.sbd.18107.shnf**: transferred by Andy Lemieux, Sean Ribss, Charlie Miller; source: SBD>Rm>Dat>Sonic Solutions>CD [4]. Also: Partial soundboard: reel to DAT, Sonic Solutions, CD, EAC, SHN, via Charlie Miller [4]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by Grateful Dead of the Day: [September 30, 1976](https://gratefuldeadoftheday.com/09-30-1976/) [21]
